statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME equity index futures halt is now twenty-five hours old and removes the very price path this score measures. Stress rises to 56 in the elevated band after three items were verified this hour: the Houthis have completed control of Yemen's Red Sea coastline including Perim island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and declared navigation unsafe for Saudi vessels, a Houthi projectile wounded two people inside Saudi Arabia, and Trump publicly attributed the East-West pipeline attack to Iran. Confidence is 87 in the high band: levels, yields, oil and the seven-day calendar were re-verified against primary sources, and the only structurally unavailable input is live price path.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and the single shared reading applies jointly to NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support that reading. First, no venue quotes the Nasdaq-100 at any point in the published horizon: CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, one hour after this horizon's final slot. A score that measures a pathological price path cannot be elevated across hours in which no path can form. Second, the last observed session granted mean reversion rather than denying it, with the index closing 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point range, while VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84 and settled near its session low. Third, the weekend escalation that lifted Stress is a supply-route and attribution story rather than observed index structure, and it is partly offset by Saudi non-retaliation at Baghdad's request, by the Houthi message that they do not seek U.S. involvement, and by Monday's scheduled Salalah meeting. No danger window is published, because no slot in this horizon contains a tradeable instrument. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unchanged.
headline: Twenty-five hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84 and WTI marked $100.05, while the Houthis complete control of Yemen's Red Sea coastline and Perim island in Bab el-Mandeb, declare navigation unsafe for Saudi vessels, and Trump attributes the shut East-West pipeline's drone attack to Iran, leaving the main Hormuz bypass impaired at both ends into Monday's reopen.
body:
The price picture is unchanged, as a closed weekend requires, and every level was re-verified against primary sources this hour. The Nasdaq-100 quote page shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high, roughly 4.5% under the 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX is 15.84, down 2.00 points or 11.21% from 17.84, having settled near the 15.59 low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range. The latest H.15 observation, for 10 September, shows the 2-year at 4.56%, the 5-year at 4.75%, the 10-year at 4.95% and the 30-year at 5.37%, with the federal funds effective rate at 3.63%. WTI is marked $100.05, down 2.37% on the day but up 9.7% on the week and 20.15% on the month, with Brent $104.61, down 2.81%.

Three developments were verified this hour and together they widen the supply-risk surface rather than the index-path risk. Reuters reporting confirms that Trump, speaking in Dublin, said of Iran's responsibility for the East-West pipeline attack, 'I think they are, probably they are', while adding that the Houthis 'would much prefer not having us involved, and they're letting most ships go through'. Separately, the Houthis have taken the port city of Mokha, the coastal town of Dhubab and Perim island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, completing control of Yemen's Red Sea coastline, with their military spokesperson stating that 'maritime navigation is safe for all companies except for Saudi vessels'. A Houthi projectile also wounded two people in Saudi Arabia's Al-Tuwal area. The material consequence is structural: with Hormuz effectively closed since February, the East-West pipeline to Yanbu was the principal bypass, and that route is now impaired at its inlet, which is shut with no published restart date, and at its Red Sea exit.

Delayed latest-session cross-asset context is consistent with Friday's verified tape rather than contradicting it: index futures closed higher across NQ, ES and YM, the volatility future fell, gold was flat, Treasury futures were marginally lower, and seven of eight megacaps and five of seven semiconductor names closed positive. That context is confirmation only and is never treated as live price-path evidence.

The assessment consequence is a widening gap between the two scores. Stress moves from 53 to 56 because the unresolved supply picture is broader than it was an hour ago and because the index will eventually meet a two-day news load it has not priced. Tail stays at 6 because every hour of the published horizon is a closed market, and event importance, attribution and headline severity raise Stress and Confidence rather than Tail until an actual price path is observable. Offsets are real and verified: Riyadh has withheld retaliation at Baghdad's request, the Houthis have signalled they do not want direct U.S. confrontation, and foreign ministers from the GCC, Iraq and Iran are due to meet in Salalah on Monday, although reporting indicates no signed Hormuz agreement is expected there. Beyond this horizon the calendar is dense, with U.S. Retail Sales and the FOMC decision, projections and press conference all falling on Wednesday 16 September.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 22:00 UTC on 11 September to 21:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens one hour into the CME halt with Tail at 6 and Stress in the elevated band at 64, still decaying from Friday's session. Tail fell to 5 by 00:00 UTC and has held a 5 to 6 band in normal mode across every remaining slot, tracking the closure rather than any directional view, which is the correct behaviour for a score that measures price path when no price path exists. Stress decayed steadily from 64 to a 50 trough at 17:00 UTC as the initial pipeline shock was absorbed, then firmed to 52 and 53 as the Qeshm Island explosions and the Salalah meeting were verified. Confidence held a narrow 85 to 88 range throughout. Every slot mapped to EA_ON and green, and no danger window was published in any of them.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, one hour after this horizon's final slot closes. Conditional Tail opens at 6 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, then steps gradually to a ceiling of 18 as unpriced weekend exposure accumulates toward the reopen. Every slot stays inside the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green throughout and no danger window is published; a slot in which no instrument trades cannot be assigned a block. Stress traces a shallow U, easing to 55 across the dead overnight hours and firming to 61 in the final slots as pre-reopen positioning meets an unresolved supply picture. The one genuine intra-horizon checkpoint is the Gulf cash session, since Tadawul opens at 07:00 UTC on Sunday and provides the first live pricing anywhere of the pipeline shutdown, the Bab el-Mandeb seizure and the U.S. attribution; that is Saudi cash equity rather than NQ, so it would inform Stress and Confidence without establishing index price-path evidence. Confidence dips to 84 through the quietest hours and rebuilds to 88 as Sunday reporting refreshes the evidence base.
